newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's communists threaten constitutional break.
newsitem.headline: Spain's communists threaten constitutional break.

text.p: Spain's communists have threatened to break with the country's constitution and promote a return to a pre-Civil War republican government.

Communist Party (PCE) chief Julio Anguita told a party meeting the PCE would free itself from the obligations of a multi-party pact supporting the 1978 constitution if the other parties continued in its opinion to lower state standards.
The PCE is the majority partner of the United Left coalition led by Anguita, which won 11 percent of the vote in the general election in March and controls 21 of parliament's 350 seats.

Anguita topped two weeks of harsh attacks on the government for defying court requests to hand over a batch of secret files with a speech late on Saturday urging supporters to band together and promote a new federal state.
He said the government should be based on the non-monarchist, republican government in place before and during the 1936-39 Civil War.
"Our formula of state is of the Republic, the PCE is Republican," Anguita told a cheering crowd of several thousand.

The PCE believes the conservative government, like the socialist one before it, breached constitutional principles by refusing to comply with court requests to declassify files on a 1980s "dirty war" on Basque rebels.
The files allegedly document the government's involvement in the 1983-87 campaign of bombings, kidnappings, torture and murder that killed 27 people, one-third of them by mistake.
